thread:
sara_sales: Hey team — ACME POC is blocked. Their generate calls keep returning 403 with an 'invalid_project_claim' message. They say the key shows active in the console. Can someone triage quickly?

devx_ian: Can you paste the exact curl and the raw error from their logs?

sara_sales: Sure — customer sent this:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: demo' \
  -d '{"model":"rw/gpt-9b","input":"hi"}'```
Response: `{"error":"invalid_project_claim","status":403,"hint":"token project 'prod' doesn't match header 'demo'"}`

chao_eng: That hint is the giveaway — token's payload claim is project=prod but header says demo. Could be they grabbed an account-wide/service key that is bound to a different project.

sara_sales: They grabbed the key from the onboarding email labeled 'demo' though. Could be stale.

devx_ian: Two quick paths: ask them to rotate/create a new project-scoped key from console (console -> Projects -> demo -> Keys -> create). Or have them remove the X-Redwood-Project header so the gateway falls back to the token claim (not ideal). Which do we prefer for a POC?

chao_eng: Recommend rotate to a project-scoped key. Also verify whether the key is an API key vs service account JWT. API keys created pre-policy-change might have been shadow/global. We rolled token policy 30m ago.

oncall_bot: deploy-bot: Token policy v2 deployed 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z — deprecated global shadow keys. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-token-groups

devx_ian: If they can't rotate immediately, we can temporarily add a routing exception for their tenant id but that requires approvals from ops/eng-infra and will be time-consuming. For POC speed, rotation is fastest.

sara_sales: Also they called earlier about intermittent 429s — likely due to client retry storm. If we fix the 403 and they replay queued requests we'll need to watch rate limits.

chao_eng: Right — 429s are separate quotas. For short term, set their quota burst to 50 and steady to 5rps in console (Projects -> demo -> Quotas). If they need sustained throughput we should propose a reserved pool (Dedicated).

devx_ian: Quick dev tip to share with them: make sure the app sets both org/project headers to match the token claims. Example:```// node example
fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_...', 'X-Redwood-Org': 'acme-corp', 'X-Redwood-Project': 'prod' } })```

sara_sales: I'm asking them to rotate and will paste new curl when they do. I captured request_id=abc-123-def from their logs and opened a support ticket.

chao_eng: If rotation fails, have them paste the JWT (only header + payload, redact signature) so we can decode claims. DO NOT paste private key material. We can also decode server-side if they send the request-id.

devx_ian: Also FYI for pricing conversation: if they hit quota after fix we should propose a trial dedicated pool (30d) — sales can draft terms. Ops, do we have quick approval path for short-term capacity?

sara_sales: I'll flag for ops if they ask. For now rotating key and re-testing is the ask. I'll update the ticket and DM when they send the new curl. :thumbsup:

oncall_bot: support-bot: ticket #SUP-2026-468 created for request_id=abc-123-def, assigned to eng-triage.

chao_eng: Thanks — standing by to decode JWT or escalate to infra if needed.

sara_sales: Great, thanks all — will follow up with customer and report back here.
